messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Problems with Parameters
parts:
Hey Mike,

I’ve been banging my head against the wall on this for a few weeks now, figured I’d finally ask for your advice!

I’m trying to take DEB parameters estimated from Jorn Bruggeman’s Debber tool (https://deb.bolding-bruggeman.com/) and apply them in NicheMapR to create plausible models for a group of given species that don’t have parameters in the AddMyPet database. I’ve written R code that randomly pulls from the distribution of possible values that Debber calculates for each species (so for a given species, I randomly pull a single value for the Arrhenius temperature from a normal distribution between the lower 2.5% and upper 97.5%, same for the log normal distribution for energy conductance, etc) and runs these parameters through the ectotherm model, then repeats with a different set of randomly drawn parameters from the distributions for these variables.

Since these are randomly drawn parameters from these distributions, I would expect to see some results where the model doesn't work. However, I’m pretty much exclusively seeing absolutely bonkers results, such as an animal burrowing underground and refusing to come out/starving to death even if burrow = 0 and maxdepth = 1 (and with rock bottom CT_mins, T_RB_min, T_B_min, and T_F_min), starting at stage 0 (egg) even if explicitly told to start at stage 3 (mature), and things like that. I’m positive this is a garbage in, garbage out problem, but for the life of me I can’t figure out what the garbage is. I’ve compared the values that come out of the random draws for species that are in the AddMyPet database to the exact values in AddMyPet and they seem approximate to each other. 

Have you seen anything like this before/is my basic premise of using Debber in this way wrong? (I can send you my code but I figured I’d ask the broader question first in case you had experienced this issue before)

Fingers crossed!

Adam

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Problems with Parameters
parts:
Hi Adam,

I only recently noted the existence of Debber and haven't really played with it. I see that it gives you a subset of parameters but not all the parameters you need, one obvious one being E_0, the energy content of the egg. If you're starting it of as an egg but it doesn't have enough energy to complete development, then you will indeed get odd looking results. But since you told it to start at stage 3, that may not be what's going wrong. Perhaps make sure first that a species that does have parameters is working properly with your script. Then only modify one parameter at a time to see where things start to go wrong. Happy to have a look at the code if you don't get anywhere. Note I'll be away for a couple of weeks though so might not get back to you for a little while.

All the best,
Mike

Thanks Mike! I'll keep at it. I'll also make sure to comment out the code in case I still need help when you get back (plus if I get it working it might be good to include for others to use as well!).

It looks like Debber does estimate E_0, it's just listed under the "traits" section instead of the "DEB parameters" section. It seems like all of the other core parameters and a lot of the thermal ones are estimated (p_Xm isn't, but I just now noticed your comments on how to calculate that here https://groups.google.com/g/nichemapr/c/uUrbSlWPxNE/m/lvNnlGLiAAAJ).

Best

messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Re: Problems with Parameters
parts:
I've finally figured out what happened here, figured I'd post it for future reference! Turns out there was a typo of a minus sign on the CT_minthresh parameter. Meaning, if CT_minthresh is supposed to = 12, it was =-12.

Adam
